date_note: The Financial Times report as relayed by Cointelegraph and crypto.news is dated 26 November; the pages give no earlier day.
exec: Crypto firms serving UK customers may face authorization rules for DeFi platforms, according to a Financial Times report.
plain: The Financial Times reports that the UK's financial regulator plans to go ahead with authorization requirements for DeFi platforms, citing the Binance theft. The FCA had not commented to Cointelegraph.

sources.name: Cointelegraph: UK regulator plans tighter DeFi rules, citing Binance hack: Report
Crypto.news: UK FCA pushes for tighter DeFi rules following Binance hack

summary: The Financial Times reported that the UK Financial Conduct Authority plans to proceed with authorization requirements for DeFi platforms, citing fraud and money laundering, according to Cointelegraph and crypto.news. Jane Moore of the FCA is quoted as saying the speed at which stolen funds move through DeFi can undermine efforts to intercept them; the Binance theft of 29 October is cited as an example. The FCA had not responded to Cointelegraph.
title: FCA reportedly plans to press ahead with DeFi authorization rules, citing the Binance theft

validation.note: Cointelegraph and crypto.news both relay one Financial Times report; the FT and the FCA's own pages were not read.

review.note: Compared FT-relayed claim, Moore, 29 Oct Binance, FCA no response, date 26 Nov against Cointelegraph and crypto.news
